scripted.text: Practise on this one. It is a form about forms. File it FOR FURTHER STUDY.
scripted.subject: paperwork
scripted.note: teaches refusal; its sign side brings "another copy" back (3.1): the line is written by writer 1 in the chains-mayor batch note until format.ts has a home for a one-branch follow-up

scripted.text: Welcome, Mayor. Please sign this to say you have read it. You haven't. Sign it.
scripted.subject: paperwork
scripted.note: teaches signing; its study side brings "another copy" back (3.1), as scripted-1

scripted.text: Let Till's Teas sponsor the clock tower. It would chime TILL'S TEAS on the hour.
scripted.subject: clocks
scripted.note: pays a fixed sum (3.1); never also in a comic deck

scripted.text: A small fruit basket for you. No reason. Perhaps more ribbon-cuttings? No reason.
scripted.subject: ribbons

scripted.text: Welcome, Governor. Your mug says GOVERNOR. Mine says HOME TIME.
scripted.subject: paperwork
scripted.note: the governor's first paper: Pruella welcomes you, dry, with an eye on an early finish (lunch is governor-3's running joke, so it is left to them); teaches nothing new. Suggested effects for build-office.py (the rules'): as scripted-2 (sign every club +1; study No change), with no follow-up. Edited by the comedy editor (was the door/sandwich line: leaned on governor-3's Pruella's lunches and ended on 'Welcome').

scripted.text: Welcome, President. I have welcomed three. I liked one.
scripted.subject: paperwork
scripted.note: the president's first paper: Mildred has seen three presidents and liked one, and never says which; teaches nothing new. Suggested effects as scripted-governor. Edited: punch moved to the last words; tagged statistic so the six scripted papers do not end on three undercuts.

runUp.text: Judge the {district} Prize Hedge Show. Say nothing about the leaning one.
runUp.subject: hedges

runUp.text: Open the {district} tea dance. Your dance card is in triplicate.
runUp.subject: ceremonies
runUp.note: replaces may-runup-pop-in (a third fête in the file; 'pop in' against four hours was mild)

runUp.text: Award {district}'s best-kept bench. Do not sit on it. It is kept.
runUp.subject: ceremonies
runUp.note: visitor Bertram Loam (slow, careful) for a face other than Rodney's

runUp.text: Wear the {district} fête sash: GUEST OF HONOUR (SELF-NOMINATED).
runUp.subject: vanity

runUp.text: Lay {district}'s first paving stone. The second says you did.
runUp.subject: vanity
runUp.note: retagged undercut (the second stone deflates the first); visitor Rodney (vanity is his)

runUp.text: Judge the {district} fruit show. Declare any baskets first.
runUp.subject: vegetable-shows
runUp.note: Gwendolyn speaks (the Treasury Clerk asks for interests declared); calls back to the first fruit basket, which every player meets at 0:38

runUp.text: Open the {district} jumble sale. Your old hat is on table three.
runUp.subject: hats

runUp.text: Tour {district}: 5 minutes for you, 15 for photographs of you.
runUp.subject: vanity
runUp.note: replaces may-runup-twenty-minutes: the same idea, with the punch in the last words

runUp.text: Lean on the {district} gate, thoughtfully. The gate is on loan.
runUp.subject: vanity
runUp.note: replaces may-runup-soup (too close to gold G8, 'say goodness, we will cue you')

runUp.text: Unveil a plaque in {district}, where you once unveiled a plaque.
runUp.subject: ceremonies
runUp.note: replaces may-runup-visitors-book (its escalation tag was not honest, and the governor run-up already signs a roll of honour)

rallies.text: A rally at the fête. The budget allows one snip. Do not miss.
rallies.subject: ribbons
rallies.note: replaces may-rally-loan-scissors ('snips are counted' read close to counting in an election paper; Gwendolyn was only implied)

rallies.text: Hold a rally at the bandstand. Bring the ceremonial scissors. Cut something.
rallies.subject: ribbons

rallies.text: A rally at the vegetable show. Cut the ribbon. Not the pumpkin.
rallies.subject: vegetable-shows
rallies.note: retagged undercut: a warning that deflates the ceremony, not a phrase taken at its word

rallies.text: A rally at the flower show. Hold the scissors up for the Drizzle. Higher. Good.
rallies.subject: ribbons
rallies.note: 'the show' made concrete; Rodney directing the photograph
